phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila miranda (1.9 µm, detail scale)

paleobiology.note: Age does not change along this extant triple. The selected wavenumber does.

equations: du/dt = D_u laplacian(u) + a - u + u^2 v
dv/dt = D_v laplacian(v) + b - u^2 v
k_max = argmax_k sigma(k), lambda = 2 pi / k_max
sigma(k) = largest real eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(D_u, D_v)
empirical_claims: Turing (1952) selects a finite wavenumber when the inhibitor diffuses farther than the activator and tr J < 0, det J > 0.
Shoup (1966) places Drosophila eye pigment granules at a sub-micron to about one-micron scale, which is the tier this 1.9 µm detail wavelength sits in.
Bachtrog (2008, 2013) documents neo-Y degeneration in Drosophila miranda. That literature does not measure a 1.9 µm Turing wavelength; the wavelength here is reconstructed.
At 0 Ma the melanogaster predecessor lattice is finer (1.412 µm) and the mojavensis successor lattice is coarser (2.286 µm) under D_u ∝ λ^2.
boundary_conditions: Periodic square of side 22.368 µm, twelve target wavelengths across.
